Electrical Engineering (PhD)
Why Pursue a PhD in Electrical Engineering
This doctoral program stresses both theoretical and practical aspects of Electrical & Computer Engineering by combining the teaching and research expertise of the university community with the resources of other San Antonio research institutions. Graduate faculty are very active in conducting cutting-edge research projects, which provide both research experiences and financial supports for graduate students.
Research Opportunities
Research in the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering mainly focuses on five concentrations:
Communications
Communications
Fiber optic communications, fiber optic sensors, coding and error correction, control of communication networks, positioning and navigation algorithms, GPS, signal processing for communications, digital communications systems, wireless mobile communications, information theory, and signal detection and estimation.
Close
Computer and Digital Systems
Computer and Digital Systems
Parallel and distributed computing, routing in computer networks, network intrusion detection, computer architecture, ASICs, RISC processors, microprocessor based systems, VLSI design and testing, CAD tools, HDL modeling and FPGA implementation, computer graphics hardware and software parallelism, visualization techniques, information science, optimization and forecasting, digital systems, multimedia and network processors, low power VLSI systems, and reconfigurable computing.
Close
Signal and Image Processing
Signal and Image Processing
Signal and image processing, visual communication, and quantum information processing and communication, signals and systems, tomographic imaging, processing biomedical images FISH (Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization), theory of fast unitary transforms, robust linear and nonlinear filters, morphological image processing, statistical signal processing, Bayesian methods, sampling-based approaches.
Close
Systems and Control
Systems and Control
Intelligent systems, neural networks and fuzzy systems, adaptive learning, data mining, networking, diagnosis and prognosis, health monitoring, and robotics and automation, Complex Systems, Computational Intelligence, System of Systems Engineering, Mechatronics, Neuro-fuzzy techniques, robotics and intelligent networks/systems, robust and adaptive control, stabilization of nonlinear systems, optimal control, homogeneous systems theory, aerospace systems and power plants.
Close
Microelectronics and Microdevices
Microelectronics and Microdevices
This concentration area provides students with balanced training in theory and experimentation in the areas of analog and mixed signal integrated circuit design, microsystems technology (MEMS), RF and Microwave devices. Research emphasis covers such diverse topics as wireless transceivers, data converters, power management, VLSI, micromirror arrays, MEMS microwave devices, Bio-MEMS, photonic crystals, microfluidics, sensor arrays, microchemical reactors, micropropulsion and energy harvesting schemes. Graduates are well qualified to seek employment in semiconductor manufacturing, aerospace, telecommunications, petrochemical industry, food and chemical processing, microelectronics research and development, health care and other industries requiring analog circuitry, sensing schemes or the application of microdevices.

Admission & Application Requirements
Applications are submitted through the UT San Antonio Graduate Application. Please upload all required documents (listed below) on your UT San Antonio Graduate Application. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure completion and submission of the application, a nonrefundable application fee, and all required supporting documents are on file with UT San Antonio by the appropriate application deadline.
Electrical Engineering (PhD)
Required Degree
Master's Degree Degree from an accredited college or university in the United States or have proof of equivalent training at a foreign institution. Applicants with a Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering or a related field will be required to complete additional coursework, totaling 75 semester credit hours.
Minimum GPA
3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) Departments may consider GPA of last 60 semester credit hours
Coursework
Completed adequate credit hours or foreign institution equivalent coursework as preparation for the program.
Transcripts*
Required from all institutions attended; international transcripts must be recorded/translated to English
Credential Evaluation
Required if you have earned university-level credit from foreign institutions. Submit an evaluation of your transcripts from FCSA or any NACES-approved credential evaluation agency.
English Language Proficiency
79 TOEFL iBT / 6.5 IELTS / Duolingo 100
For exams taken on or after January 21, 2026: We require a minimum TOEFL iBT score of 4.0.

Applicants are encouraged to have their admission file completed as early as possible. All applications, required documents and letters of recommendation, if applicable, must be submitted by 5:00 PM U.S. Central Time on the day of the deadline. Deadlines are subject to change.

Course Offerings & Schedule
This program is housed on Main campus. Our graduate courses are offered mostly in afternoon and evening. About half of courses are taught in the afternoon (2:00 PM to 5:00 PM) and another half in the evening (5:00 PM to 8:15 PM).
Frequently Asked Questions
What areas of specialization are available in UT San Antonio’s Electrical Engineering PhD?
The PhD in EE at UT San Antonio offers both theoretical and practical aspects of electrical and computing engineering, with five comprehensive concentrations:
Communications
Computer and Digital Systems
Signal and Image Processing
Systems and Control
Microelectronics and Microdevices
How long does the program take to complete?
This program typically takes about 3-5 years to complete, though timing can vary depending on the progress of research.
What are the career paths after earning a PhD in Electrical Engineering?
Graduates may choose to pursue a career in academia or industry, many becoming university professors, senior engineers, research scientists, etc.
What are the admission requirements?
This program requires a master’s degree from an accredited college or university in the United States or have proof of equivalent training at a foreign institution. 3.0 GPA (on a 4.0 scale). Departments may consider GPA of last 60 semester credit hours.
Are labs and research centers available to students?
Yes, there are more than a dozen research labs within the program available to PhD students, directed by faculty members.
Is funding offered to doctoral students?
All incoming graduate students will be automatically considered for a competitive scholarship, and if awarded will be qualified for in-state tuition (about 1/3 of out-of-state tuition). All PhD students are encouraged to contact individual professors in the area of research of your interests to seek financial support in the form of Teaching Assistantship, Research Assistantship or Monthly Stipend, since most financial support are from faculty directly.
In the News
UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods (Sept 08, 2026
A team of researchers at the University of Texas at San Antonio, led by Chen Pan, PhD, assistant professor of electrical engineering in the Klesse College of Engineering and Integrated Design, have engineered a self-sustaining flood warning system that detects local dangerous water accumulation at street-level. The system, powered by artificial intelligence, relies on solar energy harvesting to provide an off-grid system that generates its own power, as other warning systems often fail along with local power infrastructure right as severe weather hits. The field-ready prototype will provide rural and coastal areas in the state with a more reliable flood warning system.
Read the full story “UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods” to learn more about this incredible advancement.
Researchers from SwRI and UT San Antonio collaborate to study solid rocket propellants (Oct 14, 2026)
Researchers at the Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) and the UT San Antonio are working together to better understand solid rocket propellant. By learning more about how the rocket propellant burns, they hope to improve its efficiency and design for defense and aerospace applications.
